fix.evidence: dataNotes says post analytics is OFF for @arqentia. allTime, last30Days and last90Days all show 0 posts and null impressions, engagements and ER, while publishingLog shows 13 published posts. Nothing about copy, timing or format can be judged on results yet.

11 of the 13 posts were published between Aug 12 and Aug 27. September has only Sep 8 ('A sales call should not end…') and Sep 11 ('An invoice should not be paid…'), and there has been nothing since: 15 days of silence as of Sep 26. Early reply activity can't start on posts that don't exist.

fix.point: Every post uses the same format and opening, and none visibly asks for a reply.
fix.evidence: All 13 are single posts with one image, and none is a thread. 8 of 13 open with the same 'X should not / should never' frame (for example 'A sales call should not end as loose notes', 'An HVAC quote should never disappear'). The log shows about the first 200 characters of each post, and none of those excerpts contains a question. Replies are the heaviest ranking signal.

fix.point: Only the brand account posts, and the one API reply to another account failed.
fix.evidence: The brief contains only @arqentia; no account for Rafael is connected. The single failed post was a reply to another account, rejected by X's February 2026 rule on API replies, so replies to other accounts have to be made by hand. All 13 posts are in English, while the audience includes Latin America and Spanish.

actions.title: Turn on X analytics for @arqentia with a monthly spend cap
actions.detail: In Zernio, switch on post analytics for @arqentia and set a monthly X spend cap at the same time. At $0.005 per metrics read, 40 posts a month read 3 times each would cost about $0.60, plus about $0.60 to publish them. A cap of $5 to $10 leaves plenty of room. Check Zernio usage after week one to see how many reads actually happen, then adjust the cap.
actions.evidence: dataNotes: analytics is OFF. Every impression, engagement and ER field is null, and the 13 published posts in publishingLog have no metrics.

actions.title: Start posting again with at least one post every weekday
actions.detail: Queue at least one post for each weekday of the next two weeks in Zernio. Reuse the existing topics with new angles: invoice matching, sales calls into the CRM, supplier delays, removing access when staff change roles, idempotency, schema drift, HVAC scheduling. Keep links out of the main post.
actions.evidence: The last post was Sep 11, 15 days before this brief. 11 of the 13 posts in the 90-day log landed between Aug 12 and Aug 27. Four weekdays in a row were covered Aug 24–27.

actions.title: Reply to larger accounts by hand every day
actions.detail: Spend 20 minutes a day in the X app replying to 5 to 10 recent posts, ideally under an hour old, from larger AI, automation and operator accounts. Add one specific practice from Arqentia's work, such as the human approval step or idempotency keys, instead of just agreeing. The API can't do this, so it has to be manual.
actions.evidence: The only failed post in the log was an API reply to another account, rejected by X's February 2026 rule. No data in this brief measures how much reply activity grows an account; this is a practitioner heuristic.

actions.title: Connect Rafael's personal X account and post the same material as the founder
actions.detail: Connect Rafael's personal X account to Zernio. Post the same frameworks in first person (for example 'We connected supplier invoices to POs for a client and…'), and have @arqentia repost or quote those posts. Do the daily manual replies from Rafael's account where you can.
actions.evidence: audienceContext describes Rafael Schwart's personal brand, but the brief includes only @arqentia (321 followers). No data here compares founder and brand reach; this is based on the general pattern on X.

actions.title: Close alternate posts with a narrow question and answer replies in the first hour
actions.detail: End every other post with a specific question. For example, after 'An invoice should not be paid because it reached the right inbox…', ask 'What does your team check before approving an invoice today?'. Stay on X for 30 to 60 minutes after each post and answer every reply, because replies the author engages with carry the most ranking weight.
actions.evidence: 8 of 13 posts open with the same 'should not / should never' statement, and none of the roughly 200-character excerpts in the log contains a question. The log cuts the text off and analytics is off, so the endings and reply counts can't be seen.

actions.title: Turn one topic a week into a thread
actions.detail: Each week, expand one topic into a 4 to 6 post thread through Zernio (self-replies still work through the API): the problem, the rule, the fields or controls needed, how it fails, and the approval step. If you link a resource, put it in the last reply, and remember that reply is billed at the $0.20 link rate.
actions.evidence: All 13 posts are single posts with one image, and no threads appear in the log. Several excerpts are cut off in the middle of a step list, such as 'Every call, form, and chat needs four controls…' and 'Every booking should carry three fields…', which would work well as threads.

recommendations.cadence: There is no best-time data: the bestTimes sample is 0 and every weekday lift is null, so these slots are a starting point, not a finding. Weeks 1–2: one @arqentia post each weekday (5 a week) at 9:00 ET, where 8 of the 13 logged posts went out, plus one thread a week and 20 minutes a day of manual replies in the X app. From week 3, if you've kept up the weekday posts, add a second daily post that alternates between 12:00 ET (used Aug 12) and 17:00 ET (close to the Aug 14 and Aug 15 posts) to build a timing comparison. Stay on X for 30 to 60 minutes after each post to answer replies. Review timing once analytics has about 20 to 30 posts of data. At 10 posts a week with no links, publishing costs about $0.15 a week.

working.point: Links stay out of the main post.
working.evidence: All 13 logged posts have hasLink false. That avoids the reach penalty links tend to carry and the $0.20 link fee. Publishing all 13 cost about $0.20 in total (13 × $0.015). This is a process strength only, because no reach data exists to confirm it.
All 13 posts have mediaCount 1. Images can add dwell time on X, but with analytics off there is no way to tell whether these did.

working.point: Topics are specific and aimed at operators.
working.evidence: Posts name concrete controls. Examples: 'Retries are necessary. Duplicate actions are not.' (idempotency keys) and 'An invoice should not be paid because it reached the right inbox' (matching invoices to purchase orders, with a person approving). This fits the stated audience of operators and founders adopting AI, but no engagement numbers show it lands.

working.point: A weekday rhythm has been done before.
working.evidence: From Aug 24 to Aug 27 there was a post on four weekdays in a row, all at 9:00 ET ('An AI agent should not run support…', 'Your weekly report should not start…', 'When someone changes roles…', 'A supplier delay should not live…'). A weekday cadence is achievable.

recommendations.headline: Turn on post analytics for @arqentia in Zernio with a monthly spend cap, and start posting again: 13 posts went out in the last 90 days with no engagement data behind any of them, and nothing has been published since Sep 11.
recommendations.diagnosis: This brief has no engagement data. Analytics is off in Zernio, so @arqentia (321 followers) shows 0 tracked posts and null impressions, engagements and ER in every period, even though the publishing log lists 13 published posts and 1 failed post in the last 90 days. All 13 posts went out between Aug 12 and Sep 11, with 11 of them between Aug 12 and Aug 27. Nothing has been published in the 15 days since Sep 11, and nothing before Aug 12 appears in the 90-day window. The copy, format and timing notes below come from the publishing log and general X mechanics, so treat them as a starting playbook, not findings from engagement data.

experiments.test: For two weeks, alternate posts from the same topic families: one ending on a statement, the next ending on a specific question. Keep both in the same 9:00 ET slot, and answer every reply within 60 minutes.
experiments.metric: Replies per post and engagement rate on impressions (needs analytics on).
experiments.hypothesis: Posts that end with a narrow question get more replies than posts that end on a statement.

experiments.test: For three weeks, keep 9:00 ET on Mon/Wed/Fri. Move the Tue/Thu posts, alternating between 12:00 and 17:00 ET, until each slot has at least 5 posts.
experiments.metric: Impressions and engagements per post by slot, which will also fill the brief's bestTimes table (its sample is 0 today).
experiments.hypothesis: 9:00 ET is just the slot that has been used so far, not a proven best time.

experiments.test: For three weeks, publish 2 Spanish versions per week of that week's topics, adapted rather than translated word for word.
experiments.metric: Engagement rate and replies per Spanish post compared with English posts in the same weeks, plus follower change from the 321 baseline.
experiments.hypothesis: Spanish posts reach the Latin American part of the audience, which English-only posting misses.

fix.point: Engagement per post has fallen every month while the same template keeps repeating.
fix.evidence: Engagements per post were 2.0 in July, 1.6 in August and 1.2 in September. The line '8+ years shipping hardware programs inside a Fortune 500' appears in 16 posts between Jul 11 and Aug 10. After that come variants such as 'Ten years on factory floors', Boeing and NPI. The 'Five mistakes... and the fix for each' format ran 6 times, most recently in 'The AI demo you are watching was built to work' on Sep 23. The data does not prove the template caused the drop, but it is the main part of the content that has stayed the same.

There were 22 comments across 97 posts, and only 5 comments on the 22 posts of the last 30 days. Shares were 0 in the last 30 days, against 1 in the 30 days before. 29 of 97 posts got no engagement. The 8 posts that drew 2 or more comments also averaged 3.5 likes, saves and shares each, against 1.5 for the account.

fix.point: Video is the weakest format on this profile.
fix.evidence: The 19 videos averaged 36 reach and 1.4 engagements per post. The 6 videos posted since Aug 14 reached 218 people in total and earned 3 engagements. Examples: 'The automation that breaks is not the one that costs you' reached 51 people with 0 engagements, and 'You do not know which steps of your automation are safe to run twice' reached 42 with 0.

fix.point: Posts written in Arqentia's company voice got almost no distribution.
fix.evidence: 13 posts in Arqentia's voice were all published on days with 2 or 3 posts. They averaged 16 impressions, against 127 for the account. Examples: 'Build or buy is the wrong first question' (12 impressions), 'Kenco put six AI agents' (17) and 'Standing access gives an AI agent...' (18 impressions, 1 reach). 'One clean AI run proves possibility' (Sep 6, 9am) shows 0 impressions.

actions.title: Write two career-and-skill posts a week
actions.detail: Each week, write two posts that take a position on what an operator should learn, skip or change in their own job with AI. Model them on 'The most valuable AI skill right now is not prompting' and the 30-day plan in 'You do not need a CS degree to become an AI architect'. Tell the reader what to do, not only what you learned: 'AI is not coming for your job' was about your own career change, reached 217 people and got 0 engagements. Use factory examples as proof inside the post, not as the opening line.
actions.evidence: The 6 career and skill posts averaged 4.2 engagements per post, against 1.7 for the account. Leaving out Jul 10, they averaged 118 reach per post, against 78. The group includes both the top post by reach (Jul 10, 1,580 reach) and the top post by engagement (Aug 10, 10 engagements).

actions.title: End each post with a question and reply to comments in the first hour
actions.detail: End every post with one question that a reader can answer in a single line from their own work, for example 'Which step in your process would you never hand to a model?'. Reply to every comment within the hour it arrives. Before each post goes live, spend 15 minutes leaving real comments on posts by the operators and AI buyers you want to reach. That last step is a common LinkedIn practice, not something this data tested.
actions.evidence: There were only 22 comments across 97 posts, 5 of them in the last 30 days, and 0 shares in the last 30 days. The 8 posts with 2 or more comments averaged 3.5 likes, saves and shares each, against 1.5 for the account. Examples: 'The most valuable AI skill...' (4 comments, 10 engagements), 'Small businesses do not need an AI employee' (2 comments, 7 engagements) and 'Who runs your AI automation when you are not there?' (2 comments, 6 engagements).

actions.title: Pause video for four weeks and use those slots for text-only posts
actions.detail: Take the ideas planned as videos and publish them as text-only posts. Keep a single image only for frameworks and checklists, where images turn reach into engagement better.
actions.evidence: Video averaged 36 reach and 1.4 engagements per post, and the last 6 videos earned 3 engagements in total. Text averaged 106 reach per post (125 in September) and accounts for 6 of the 12 highest-reach posts.

actions.title: Stop posting at 11am every day: post Friday to Monday around midday and skip Tuesday and Thursday
actions.detail: Change the Zernio queue slots to Mon 12–3pm, Fri 12–3pm, Sat 9am–12pm and Sunday morning, plus an optional Wed 12–3pm. Drop Tuesday and Thursday, and spend that time replying to comments.
actions.evidence: 26 of the 30 posts since Aug 20 went out at 11am. The best time slots are Mon 12–3pm (lift 1.6, 2 posts), Fri 12–3pm (1.4, 3 posts) and Sat 9am–12pm (1.3, 8 posts). By day, Tue and Thu both sit at 0.8. 7 of the 9 posts with 5 or more engagements went out Friday to Sunday. Each slot rests on only 2–8 posts, so check again after four weeks.

actions.title: Post once a day at most, in the first person, and move company posts to the Arqentia page
actions.detail: Put 'we' and Arqentia announcements, such as 'Arqentia amplía su cobertura...' and 'At Arqentia, we would define...', on the company page. If one needs to appear here, reshare it with a one-line personal comment. Also open the Sep 6, 9am post 'One clean AI run proves possibility': it shows 0 impressions, so check that it actually published.
actions.evidence: The 13 company-voice posts, all on days with 2–3 posts, averaged 16 impressions against 127 for the account. 'How are you today? Tell us what you want to hear from us' got 81 impressions and 0 engagements.

recommendations.cadence: Post 4–5 times a week, never more than once a day, always in the first person. Use Mon 12–3pm (lift 1.6, 2 posts) and Fri 12–3pm (1.4, 3 posts) for the two career and skill posts. Add Sat 9am–12pm (1.3, 8 posts), which has the most posts behind it of any slot, and Sunday (day lift 1.2 across 13 posts; no single Sunday slot stands out, so keep it late morning). Add an optional Wed 12–3pm post to test whether weak midweek results (Tue 0.8, Wed 0.9, Thu 0.8) come from the day itself or from the 11am time used on 26 of the last 30 posts. Each slot's lift rests on only 2–8 posts, so check again after four weeks.

working.point: Posts that tell operators what to learn or skip in their own AI career get read and answered.
working.evidence: Six posts fit this pattern: 'Anthropic is turning Claude into a career ladder', 'You do not need a CS degree to become an AI architect', 'You picked your workflow...', 'AI is not coming for your job', 'Everyone is asking what new skill to learn' and 'The most valuable AI skill right now is not prompting'. Together they earned 25 engagements, or 4.2 per post against 1.7 for the account. Without the Jul 10 breakout they still averaged 118 reach per post, against 78 for the account. The group includes the biggest post by reach (Jul 10: 2,197 impressions and 1,580 reach, 21% of all-time reach) and the top post by engagement (Aug 10: 10 engagements from 5 likes, 4 comments and 1 save).

working.point: Text-only posts get the widest distribution.
working.evidence: The 17 text posts averaged 106 reach. Images averaged 57 (leaving out Jul 10), the 4 carousels 87 and video 36. Six of the 12 highest-reach posts are text, including 'You are pasting the summary into Claude' (231), 'AI is not coming for your job' (217) and 'You can build a working AI automation in Claude in one afternoon' (198). In September, text posts averaged 125 reach against about 50 for images. One caveat: images turn reach into engagement better, 3.1% against 1.4% on reach (leaving out Jul 10).

working.point: Posts published Friday through Monday do best.
working.evidence: 7 of the 9 posts with 5 or more engagements went out Friday to Sunday. One went out on a Monday (Aug 10, 1pm) and one on a Wednesday. None went out on a Tuesday or Thursday. By day, the lift is Sat 1.3 (12 posts) and Sun 1.2 (13 posts), against Tue 0.8 (11 posts) and Thu 0.8 (16 posts).

recommendations.headline: Replace the daily 11am factory-lesson post with 4–5 posts a week that tell operators what to learn or skip in their own AI work and ask them to answer. The six posts that did this averaged 4.2 engagements, against 1.7 for the account overall and 1.2 in the last 30 days.
recommendations.diagnosis: The profile posts almost every day (89 posts in 90 days; 26 of the 30 posts since Aug 20 went out at 11am). Even so, a typical post reaches about 50 people, which is under 2% of 3,566 followers, and gets 1 engagement (median). 29 of the 97 posts got no engagement at all. Two things are falling together. Reach per post went from 70 in July (leaving out the Jul 10 breakout) to 69 in August and 58 in September. Engagements per reach went from 2.7% to 2.3% to 2.0%. As a result, engagements per post fell from 2.0 to 1.6 to 1.2, no post has passed 3 engagements since Aug 15, and shares were 0 in the last 30 days. Distribution figures here are calculated on reach, while the brief's own rates use impressions. Only posts published through Zernio are counted, and per-post numbers are small, so the patterns below rely on groups of posts, not single posts.

experiments.test: For 4 weeks, alternate two kinds of posts in the same time slots. Half open with one specific incident (a date, a number, what broke, what it cost) and have no credential line in the first three lines. The other half keep the current opening.
experiments.metric: Engagements per reach and comments per post for each kind, compared with the September baseline of 2.0% on reach and 0.26 comments per post.
experiments.hypothesis: The repeated opening (a factory credential in the first lines, or 'Five mistakes... and the fix for each') is part of why engagement per post fell from 2.0 to 1.2.

experiments.test: For the next 8 posts, alternate text-only and text-with-image versions of the same kinds of post (career or skill takes, and frameworks), in the same time slots.
experiments.metric: Median reach per post and engagements per post. Baseline: text 106 reach and 1.5 engagements; image 57 reach and 1.8 engagements (leaving out Jul 10).
experiments.hypothesis: On this profile, a text-only post reaches about twice as many people as the same kind of post with an image, and gets at least as many engagements in total.

experiments.test: Over two weeks, publish 2 first-person posts ('I', not 'we'), each about one concrete workflow such as lead intake, invoices or dispatch. Make each the only post that day, in the Fri 12–3pm or Sat 9am–12pm slot.
experiments.metric: Reach, and engagements per reach, compared with three earlier posts: 'Small businesses do not need an AI employee' (7 engagements on 24 reach), 'Most businesses do not need an AI accountant' (4 on 25) and 'Most small businesses do not lose because they lack leads' (6 on 25). Those three combined converted 23% of reach, against 2.2% for the account.
experiments.hypothesis: First-person posts about one broken small-business workflow already turn reach into engagement unusually well, and will also reach more people when published alone in a top slot.

fix.point: @arqentia.inc posted less in September and its reach fell
fix.evidence: 5 posts in September against 15–17 in each of June, July and August, and nothing since Sep 19. Median reach in the last 30 days was 73 (7 posts), down from 120 in the 30 days before (13 Arqentia posts). Engagements per post fell from 13.6 to 8.1 and comments fell to 0.

fix.point: On @arqentia.inc, single-industry content does worse, and in September it made up most of the posts
fix.evidence: By my read of the captions, 12 Reels are built around one industry (HVAC, gym, restaurant, body shop, therapy, shipping, among others). Their median is 6 engagements, against 11 for the 27 owner-level Reels, and none passed 300 reach. September's 'Una silla vacía…' (dental, reach 13) and 'Lunes, 7:45 a.m.…' (pharmacy, reach 19) are the two lowest-reach posts in the account's history.

fix.point: On @arqentia.inc, 'comment' calls to action aren't producing comments, and saves are near zero
fix.evidence: 16 comments across 55 posts, 9 of them on 'Your business doesn't have a software problem…' (Jul 25). 'La meta no es trabajar más horas… Coméntalo' got 0 comments on 548 reach. The guide offer in 'Es lunes a las 9…' got 3 comments on 537 reach. Saves total 8, or 0.10% of reach.

fix.point: @rgschwart, the account with the reach, is idle and has never posted a Reel
fix.evidence: 0 posts in the last 30 days and 5 posts since Nov 2025: 4 carousels and 1 image. Its one work-focused post, 'Quick Business Trip to the Windy City…' (Nov 14), had its lowest engagement (89, 6.0% of reach). That is a single post, so read it as a caution, not a rule.

actions.title: Write the next 6 Reels as owner-level reframes, not industry case studies
actions.detail: Over the next two weeks, open each Reel with one claim any owner recognizes, shown as on-screen text in the first 2 seconds and repeated in the caption's first line. Then state the cost, then the fix, the way 'Your business doesn't have a software problem…' and 'OpenAI y Anthropic pagan…' do. Use industries only as examples inside the Reel, never as the hook. Keep posting in both Spanish and English. Before copying the top four, check whether any of them was boosted. The brief doesn't say, and their impressions-to-reach ratios (1.8–3.0) are higher than a typical Reel's (about 1.2–1.5).
actions.evidence: Owner-level Reels have a median of 11 engagements (27 posts) against 6 for single-industry Reels (12 posts), and all four posts above 500 reach used an owner-level hook. The Sep 9 dental and Sep 10 pharmacy posts reached 13 and 19 accounts.

actions.title: Co-publish Arqentia Reels as Collab posts with @rgschwart
actions.detail: Add @rgschwart as collaborator on 1 Arqentia Reel a week, with Rafael on camera speaking in the first person. Start by re-cutting the topic of 'Your business doesn't have a software problem' or 'OpenAI y Anthropic pagan $287.000'. Stop after 2 if engagement on them falls well below @rgschwart's median of 125; its one work-only post got 89.
actions.evidence: @rgschwart's median reach is 1,347 per post (5 posts), against 110 for @arqentia.inc (55 posts), and it has 3,232 followers against 121. Collab posts have never been tried on either account, so the reach gain is unproven.

actions.title: Post on @rgschwart every two weeks and let the work show
actions.detail: Post next by Oct 4. Follow the shape of the Aug 26 post: photos from the last two weeks plus 2–3 lines on what you're building and what's hard. Don't pitch. One mention of the work is enough; leave the business explainers to Arqentia.
actions.evidence: 0 posts in the last 30 days and 2 in the last 90. Engagement went 89, 114, 125, 129, 176. 'This has been one of the busiest summers…' got 176 engagements and 7 shares, while the work-only Windy City post got 89. With only 5 posts, treat this as a direction, not a finding.

actions.title: Stop single-image posts and cap carousels at one a week
actions.detail: Move image slots to Reels. Keep one carousel a week, built like 'La meta no es trabajar más horas' (broad claim, then the cost, then 'tú solo apruebas') and posted Saturday afternoon, as a test of whether Sep 19 repeats. Don't post more single-industry carousels (dental, pharmacy, the AC checklist) until then.
actions.evidence: Images: 9 posts, median reach 34. Carousels: 7 posts, median reach 23, including the broad 'Most teams do not have a reporting problem…' (23) and '7 of 10 after-hours calls…' (34). Only Sep 19 broke out, at 548.

actions.title: Ask for shares, not comments, on the reach posts
actions.detail: End owner-level Reels by asking viewers to send the post on, for example 'Mándaselo a tu socio' or 'Send this to whoever runs your ops'. Keep the comment-KEYWORD call to action for one lead-magnet post a week. Judge that post on shares, saves, reach and the DMs it produces (tracked outside this brief), not on comment count.
actions.evidence: 0 comments across 7 posts in the last 30 days. 'Coméntalo' on the Sep 19 post got 0 comments on 548 reach. The one post that stated a principle, 'Most of the time, the problem is within the process design…', drew 20 of the account's 49 all-time shares.

recommendations.cadence: @arqentia.inc: 4 posts a week (3 Reels, 1 carousel), up from 5 posts in all of September and none since Sep 19. Slots: Sat 3–6pm (lift 1.5 on 3 posts: 'Es lunes a las 9…' 31, 'La meta no es…' 27, 'You didn't start this business' 10, all at or above the median of 9), Tue 6–9pm (lift 1.2, 4 posts), Wed 6–9pm (1.1, 2 posts) and Thu 12–3pm (1.0, 3 posts). Sat 6–9am also shows 1.5, but that rests on the Jul 25 post alone; the other two there got 9 and 4. Skip Friday (0.8 over 10 posts). The hour matters less than the hook here: 7–8am Reels had a median reach of 113, against 120 at other hours. @rgschwart: 1 post every two weeks. Its two Saturday posts landed at its median (125, 129) and its best post went out Wed 10am (176), so either slot works. The best-time table pools both accounts with only 2–4 posts per slot, so re-check it after 4 weeks.

working.point: On @arqentia.inc, owner-level reframe hooks are what reach beyond the followers
working.evidence: All four posts above 500 reach open on a claim any owner recognizes: 'Your business doesn't have a software problem…' (Jul 25: 767 reach, 58 engagements, 6.4x the median of 9), 'OpenAI y Anthropic pagan $287.000…' (Aug 6: 724, 49), 'La meta no es trabajar más horas…' (Sep 19: 548, 27) and 'Es lunes a las 9 y estás comprando leads…' (Aug 8: 537, 31). Together they produced 2,576 of the account's 7,683 all-time reach. Three of the four are in Spanish, though only 13 of the 55 posts are.

working.point: On @arqentia.inc, Reels are the only format that regularly gets past the 121 followers
working.evidence: 39 Reels: median reach 118, median 9 engagements. 7 carousels: median reach 23, median 5 engagements. 9 images: median reach 34, median 7 engagements.

working.point: On @arqentia.inc, a post that states a principle earned shares (sends), the signal Instagram weights most for reaching non-followers
working.evidence: 'Most of the time, the problem is within the process design…' (Jun 16) got 20 shares on 118 reach, or 17% sends per reach. That is 20 of the account's 49 all-time shares. Without it, the account's share rate is 0.38% of reach.

Engagements went 89, 114, 125, 129, 176 across its 5 posts (Nov 2025 to Aug 2026). 'This has been one of the busiest summers…' (Aug 26) got 176 engagements, which is 1.4x its median of 125 and 13.1% of reach. It also got 7 of the account's 16 all-time shares. Median reach is 1,347, or 42% of 3,232 followers.

recommendations.headline: On @arqentia.inc, go back to owner-level reframe Reels and stop leading with a single industry: all four posts that passed 500 reach opened on a claim any owner recognizes, while September's dental and pharmacy carousels reached 13 and 19 accounts.
recommendations.diagnosis: @arqentia.inc depends on a few owner-level posts. Four of its 55 posts produced 34% of its 7,683 all-time reach, and the rest sit near the median reach of 110, which is close to its 121 followers. In September that went the wrong way: the account posted 5 times (it had posted 15–17 times in each of June, July and August), leaned on single-industry Peru content and carousels, and saw median reach fall from 120 to 73 and comments fall to 0. @rgschwart is the opposite: it has 27x the followers, a median reach of 1,347 per post and engagement that rises with every post (89 to 176), but it hasn't posted since Aug 26 and has never posted a Reel. Rates here are on reach (Arqentia 8.2%, @rgschwart 9.8% all-time) rather than the brief's impressions basis (6.5%, 3.3%), because @rgschwart's carousels log about 3.3 impressions per account reached. The brief has no watch time, no follower-vs-non-follower split and no follower growth, and @rgschwart has only 5 posts, so data quality is limited.

experiments.test: Over the next 2 weeks, publish 2 Collab Reels with owner-level hooks and Rafael on camera, Saturday 3–6pm. Publish 2 solo Arqentia Reels in the same weeks to compare against.
experiments.metric: Reach against 110 (Arqentia median) and 1,347 (@rgschwart median); shares per reach; new @arqentia.inc followers in the 48 hours after each post.
experiments.hypothesis: Arqentia Reels posted as Collab posts with @rgschwart will reach well above Arqentia's median of 110 without falling far below @rgschwart's usual engagement.

experiments.test: Publish 2 Spanish carousels with the same structure (broad claim, cost, 'tú solo apruebas') on Saturday 3–6pm on consecutive weeks.
experiments.metric: Reach against the carousel median of 23; impressions-to-reach ratio (Sep 19 was 2.97, a sign Instagram showed it again); saves plus shares per reach.
experiments.hypothesis: The Sep 19 carousel's 548 reach came from its broad claim and its Saturday-afternoon slot, not from chance.

experiments.test: Publish 1 personal Reel (15–30 seconds, a real workday, hook as on-screen text in the first 2 seconds) within the next 2 weeks, in place of one carousel.
